Quick triage update — top-line findings below.

What I ran: dig +trace against hawthorne inference hostnames from our us-west-2 edge and a probe in the customer VPC. Captured proxy headers and edge logs.

Findings:
- Several DNS responses from the customer's authoritative view are resolving the inference host to an internal proxy IP (10.10.45.7) for a subset of lookups. This appears split-horizon: from Hawthorne's peered VPC the name resolves to their internal proxy, while public resolution returns our normal edge IPs.
- Requests that resolve to 10.10.45.7 are hitting Hawthorne's proxy which is returning 502s under load (their proxy is not configured to stream large responses / chunked).
- Our us-west-2 edge shows an uptick in retries to the same upstream IP; p99 increases correlate with proxy timeouts and connection resets.

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Request Hawthorne to update their split-horizon DNS so inference hostnames resolve to our public edge from the peered VPC (fast but needs their network change).
2) Create a routing override at our edge for Hawthorne's peer to force egress through an alternate path that bypasses their proxy (we can push a temporary host-route + header flag). Risk: requires change to routing policy and short rollback window.
3) Failover selected customers to our dedicated pool in us-east-1 (no DNS change needed). This is safest but will add cross-region latency.

I attached a dns-trace.zip with traces and our edge logs. I'm going to open INF-7219 in Jira and tag network on-call.

Monica
